sample.name: War Memorial Veterans Building Herbst Theatre
facts: The United Nations Charter was signed on its stage on June 26, 1945.
Renamed in 1977 for brothers Herman and Maurice Herbst, whose foundation paid for renovations.
Opened in 1915

sample.name: Bayview Opera House Ruth Williams Memorial Theatre
facts: Built in 1888 and reputed to be the oldest existing theatre in San Francisco.
Renamed in 1995 for playwright and actress Ruth Williams, who helped prevent its demolition.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2011.

sample.name: The Independent
facts: Opened in its current form on Feb. 27, 2004.
The space was earlier the Half Note jazz club, the Kennel Club and the Justice League.
Address: 628 Divisadero Street, San Francisco

sample.name: Roxie
facts: Has operated under the name Roxie since 1933.
Four film lovers bought and remodeled it as an independent film center in March 1976.
Operates as a nonprofit arthouse cinema.

sample.name: Bill Graham Civic Auditorium
facts: Built in 1915 as part of the Panama-Pacific International Exposition.
Renamed in 1992 for rock promoter Bill Graham.
Hosted the 1920 Democratic National Convention.

sample.name: Orpheum Theatre
facts: Opened in 1926 as the Pantages Theatre, designed by B. Marcus Priteca.
The facade is patterned after a 12th-century French cathedral.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 94.

sample.name: Victoria Theatre
facts: Built in 1908 as Brown's Opera House.
Named a San Francisco Designated Landmark (no. 215) in 1996.
It is the oldest operational theatre in San Francisco.

sample.name: Brava Theater Center
facts: The theater has 360 seats.
It is dedicated to the expression of women, people of color, youth and LGBTQ artists.
Address: 2781 24th Street, San Francisco

sample.name: San Francisco Zoo
facts: Fleishhacker bought a 30-acre site from the Spring Valley Water Company in 1922.
The first major exhibits were built in the 1930s by the Works Progress Administration.
Founded in 1929

sample.name: Presidio Theatre
facts: Built in 1939 as the Presidio's first dedicated movie theatre.
Was funded through the Works Progress Administration.
Reopened in September 2019 after a rehabilitation funded by the Margaret E. Haas Fund.

sample.name: Club Fugazi
facts: Opened in 1913 inside Casa Fugazi, a community center for San Francisco's Italian colony.
Thelonious Monk recorded the album Thelonious Alone in San Francisco here in 1959.
Beach Blanket Babylon played here until its final show in December 2019.

sample.name: Curran Theatre
facts: Opened in February 1922 and named for its first owner, Homer Curran.
Architect Alfred Henry Jacobs designed it.
Hosted pre-Broadway runs including Fences in 1987 and Wicked in 2003.

sample.name: Warfield Theatre
facts: Opened May 13, 1922 as the Loews Warfield, a vaudeville theater.
Named after the actor David Warfield.
Reopened in September 2008 as a live music venue.
